tome.research.constellation.astralsorcer: Creation
The stars of growth. Where this light falls, living things flourish. Its lumen is drawn from the Hyacinth, and those attuned to it grow stronger by building.
Defense
The stars of defence. Its light hardens whatever it settles on. Its lumen is drawn from the Orchid, and those attuned to it grow stronger by enduring harm.
Offense
The stars of force. Its light sharpens and drives. Its lumen is drawn from the Thistle, and those attuned to it grow stronger by dealing harm.
Destruction
The stars of breaking. Its light wears away what it touches and quickens the hand that breaks. Its lumen is drawn from the Protea, and those attuned to it grow stronger by breaking.
Motion
The stars of motion. Its light hastens whatever moves beneath it. Its lumen is drawn from the Iris, and those attuned to it grow stronger by travelling.
Light
A minor constellation whose light is far brighter than its distance should allow, bright enough to be mistaken for day. Its focus is what makes the Illumination Wand.
Mineral
A minor constellation. Beneath its light the stone of the world shifts and changes over time. Its uses are still being uncovered.
Time
A minor constellation that keeps to its own schedule and appears only rarely. Its light bends time around whatever it falls on.
Ocean
A minor constellation. Beneath its light water stirs and the life within it multiplies.
Herding
A minor constellation whose gentle light keeps animals calm and well.
Heat
A minor constellation. A fierce heat follows close behind its light.
Convocation
A minor constellation seen only on the darkest and the brightest of nights. Its light draws creatures toward it with an unnatural pull.
tome.research.lumen.astralsorcery.aevita: <color="#55FF55">Aevitas</color> is the aspect of growth and life. A body bound with it endures more than it should. It is drawn from the Hyacinth. Bound into a flask it gives Regeneration. Its bindings are fed by the harm you take, so it suits those who expect to be struck.
tome.research.lumen.astralsorcery.armara: <color="#55FF55">Armara</color> is the aspect of defence. It hardens armour it is bound to, and a bound weapon or tool has a chance to turn a blow aside entirely. It is drawn from the Orchid. Bound into a flask it gives Resistance. Its bindings are fed by the harm you take.
tome.research.lumen.astralsorcery.discid: <color="#55FF55">Discidia</color> is the aspect of force and offence. It sharpens every strike, whether from a blade, a bow, or a tool turned to violence. It is drawn from the Thistle. Bound into a flask it gives Strength. Its bindings are fed by the harm you deal.
tome.research.lumen.astralsorcery.evorsi: <color="#55FF55">Evorsio</color> is the aspect of breaking. It quickens the hand that breaks stone, and on a weapon it drives through armour instead. It is drawn from the Protea. Bound into a flask it gives Haste. Its bindings are fed by breaking blocks, or by the harm a bound weapon deals.
<color="#55FF55">Vicio</color> is the aspect of motion. It speeds your step, and on a bow it speeds the arrow instead. It is drawn from the Iris. Bound into a flask it gives Speed. Its bindings are fed by travel, or by the harm a bound bow deals.
<color="#55FF55">Virel</color> is life joined to motion, the first of the combined aspects. Everything bound with it moves faster and lasts longer. Bound into a flask it gives Regeneration. Its bindings are fed by the harm you take and by travel.
<color="#55FF55">Solyn</color> is life joined to defence. It gives life and armour to what it protects, marks whatever it strikes so the mark can be seen through walls, and a tool bound with it leaves small lights behind in the dark as it works. Bound into a flask it gives Resistance. Its bindings are fed by the harm you take.
tome.research.lumen.astralsorcery.nullae: <color="#55FF55">Nullae</color> is breaking joined to motion, the aspect of the miner. Armour and tools bound with it break faster and move faster, and its blades reach farther and pierce armour. Bound into a flask it gives Blindness, with Haste following once the darkness lifts. Its bindings are fed by breaking, by travel, and by the harm its weapons deal.
tome.research.lumen.astralsorcery.caldor: <color="#55FF55">Caldor</color> is force, defence, and breaking joined into pure aggression. It lengthens reach, drives through armour, and an arrow bound with it never strays from its mark. Bound into a flask it gives Invisibility. Its bindings are fed by harm taken and dealt, and on a tool by breaking.
tome.research.lumen.astralsorcery.hyle.d: <color="#55FF55">Hyle</color> is the bulwark, made from Solyn, Virel, and Armara. Armour bound with it takes less harm and shields the wearer when struck hard. Blades bound with it draw life from what they cut. A tool bound with it breaks a wide face at once. Bound into a flask it gives strong Resistance.
tome.research.lumen.astralsorcery.dynami: <color="#55FF55">Dynamis</color> is fury, made from Solyn, Virel, and Vicio. It quickens every attack and every swing, makes strikes land true and hard, and a killing blow from a blade bound with it bursts outward against everything near. Bound into a flask it gives Rampage.
tome.research.lumen.astralsorcery.aion.d: <color="#55FF55">Aion</color> is the aspect of time, made from Nullae, Caldor, and Discidia. Everything bound with it recovers sooner. Blows against you lengthen the blessings you carry. Blades slow what they strike. A tool bound with it hastens the crops around each one it harvests. Bound into a flask it gives Phoenix Blessing.
tome.research.lumen.astralsorcery.akasha: <color="#55FF55">Akasha</color> is the aspect of space, made from Nullae, Caldor, and Evorsio. It extends reach and step and softens falls. A tool bound with it breaks wide and gathers everything it takes into a single bundle, at no cost in lumen. Arrows bound with it never stray. Bound into a flask it gives Night Vision, with Luck following after.
tome.research.lumen.astralsorcery.prisma: <color="#55FF55">Prismatic</color> lumen is starlight with every aspect restored, made from all four of the third rank. It gives no strength of its own. Bound beside another lumen it strengthens that binding, and is spent only a little as that binding is spent. Bound into a flask it deepens and lengthens whatever the flask already holds, once only. It is also the price of the greatest infusion.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.welcome:
You opened it, which is a better start than most manage. Sit down.
The <color="#55FFFF">Tome</color> in your hands is not like your other books. It will learn from you as you learn from it. As your understanding of the sky grows, so will its pages. The things that you are not yet ready to grasp, it will not yet show you. Consider that a kindness rather than an insult.
I have been reading the night sky for longer than you would believe. Through this manuscript you will learn what I have learned.

Close these pages and you will find a chart of everything I mean to teach you. Each entry is a lesson to be experienced. The lines between them are the order I would take them in, and some entries stay dark until you have earned them.
Your first task is modest. Learn where the useful stones of your world hide, find the light that falls on it at night, and build yourself a proper table to work at. Do that and your vision will expand, and this book with it.
Not every stone listens to the sky. <color="#55FF55">Marble</color> does. Your world keeps it in pale veins through ordinary rock, from well beneath the surface up into the hills, and even a common stone pick is enough to gather it.
Cut it into the forms shown on the pages that follow. The shapes are not only for looks. Later constructions demand particular forms in particular places, and the marble will know if you cheat.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.sooty_m:
Marble takes on more than dirt when you rub it with coal. The soot goes into the stone and stays there, and what you get is a darker surface that holds light instead of reflecting it back.
You will want a great deal of it in time. The larger works you build later stand on floors of <color="#55FF55">Sooty Marble</color>, and nothing else will do. It cuts into the same shapes as its paler cousin.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.constel:
Your world has forgotten most of what it once knew about the sky. A few scraps survive buried in time. Look for <color="#55FF55">Constellation Paper</color> in the old places, in strongholds, temples, sunken ships, buried chests, and whatever ruins nobody visits twice.
A fresh paper is blank and faintly sparkling. Once you pick it up a drawing appears on it, always of a <color="#55FFFF">constellation</color> you have not yet seen.

<color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> the paper to study it. You will see the pattern of stars and the phases of the moon during which it hangs overhead. Note the phases. The sky keeps a schedule and not all constellations will always be visible each night.
Memorizing a drawing is not the same as finding it in the sky. That takes an <color="#55FF55">Astrolabe</color> and a clear night.
Once a constellation is in your memory, the Tome keeps a copy. <color="#FFFF55">Sneak + Right-click</color> the Tome to take out a fresh paper whenever you need one.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.ores.te:
<bold>Aquamarine Shale</bold>
Where water runs slow over sand, the starlight collects as small gifts. Look along riverbeds and shallow shores for lone blocks of pale shale. They crumble like sand, and a stone shovel or better takes them apart. Inside is <color="#55FF55">Aquamarine</color>, a stone that remembers the light it soaked up. Much of what you make in the early days starts with a piece of it.

<bold>Rock Crystal Ore</bold>
Far below, near the floor of the world, pressure grows crystals that have never seen open air. They are always buried, so you will dig blind or learn to listen for them. A <color="#55FF55">Resonating Wand</color> in hand will show you where.
Bring an iron pick or better and break the ore yourself. <color="#FF5555">Be warned, crystals freed with no one near to catch them are lost.</color> Each <color="#55FF55">Rock Crystal</color> comes out different from the last. You will learn to care about that in time.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.astrola:
You cannot learn the sky by squinting at it. The <color="#55FF55">Astrolabe</color> is a glass built for the purpose. Raise it to your eye and the stars will come into view.
Along the left edge sits a rule of angles with a small marker on it. Roll your <color="#FFFF55">mouse wheel</color> while looking through the glass to raise or lower the marker. The angle you choose matters more than it seems. I will explain why shortly.

To find a <color="#55FFFF">constellation</color>, wait for a clear night when the moon is in the right phase, then hold <color="#FFFF55">Sneak</color> while you look through the glass. Your hand steadies and you may draw. Drag a line from one star to the next, following the drawing on your paper, until every connection is traced.
Get it right and the pattern is <color="#55FFFF">discovered</color>, and you will recognize it in the night sky from now on. Get it wrong and nothing happens. Release Sneak to clear the lines and try again. The brightest constellations will be visible first. The dimmer ones are not yet within your reach.

There is more in the glass than stars. Scattered across your world are places where the light of a single constellation falls to the ground. I call them <color="#55FFFF">focal points</color>. You will know one by the bare patch it leaves in the grass.
At night, with the glass raised and your marker near the right angle, a column of light rises there. Look at it directly and it stays recorded in your memory. Find one. Everything that follows happens beneath it.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.wand.te:
Now for the trick of it. Starlight falling on a <color="#55FFFF">focal point</color> is enough to remake certain things, if you leave them in it long enough.
Throw the ingredients on the open ground at the focal point, all in one pile, and step back. Sparks gather over the pile. Leave it be. When the light is done, a <color="#55FF55">Resonating Wand</color> lies where the pile was. <color="#FF5555">If you disturb the pile, the work is lost.</color>

The wand is a tuning fork for starlight. It has a few habits worth knowing.
Hold it and walk the deep places. Buried <color="#55FF55">Rock Crystal</color> answers with a sparkle you can see through solid stone.
<color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> a starlight device holding ingredients and the wand tells it to begin.
<color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> a device that wants a structure built around it and the wand draws a ghost of whatever is missing. You will thank it for that more than once.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.illumin:
Your ordinary crafting table is a fine thing for wood and iron, but it is deaf to the stars above. Leave one at a <color="#55FFFF">focal point</color>, in a pile of <color="#55FF55">Marble</color>, and the light will teach it to listen.
The same rule applies as before. One pile on open ground, and patience. What you get back is an <color="#55FF55">Illuminated Crafting Table</color>. Take it in hand and your sight will widen. New pages open in this book the moment you hold it.

Set the table anywhere you like. It needs no structure around it and, for now, preferably somewhere with a nice view of the sky. <color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> it with anything but the wand to open it and lay out your ingredients.
Its work is done by night. Wait for dark, then touch the table with the <color="#55FF55">Resonating Wand</color>. The product is thrown out on top when it finishes.
A word before you go. Other things left in the light of a focal point change too, given time. Iron ore, for instance.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.lightwe:
Crystals and Aquamarine have soaked up starlight all their lives, and they will give it back as a liquid if you know how to extract it. The <color="#55FF55">Lightwell</color> is the vessel for bringing it out.
<color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> the well with a crystal or an Aquamarine to set it in the basin. From then on the starlight within it will slowly bleed out as <color="#55FFFF">Liquid Starlight</color>, and you may draw it off with a bucket.

Understand that the well keeps what you give it. The catalyst cannot be taken back, and in time it will crumble away to nothing. A crystal of finer quality will last longer and give more freely, so choose what you place with some care.
Keep the space above the basin open. Anything set over it will shatter the catalyst at once. Pipes may draw from the underside of the well if you have them. Other materials will weep other things in the well. Netherrack gives lava, and ice gives water.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.liquid_:
Starlight in liquid form is thicker than water and glows with its own light. Step into a pool and you will sink to the bottom, and while you stand there the dark will open up to your eyes as if it were day. It does you no harm.
Its true worth is in what it does to things dropped into it. Throw an item into a pool and watch. If the starlight has an opinion about it, the pool will show you.

A single crystal left in a pool will grow, its size swelling by a step as the pool is drained into it. A young crystal takes to this readily. One already grown past its nature becomes stubborn, and the pool may be spent for nothing.
Two crystals in the same pool will merge into one. The greater of the pair absorbs some of the qualities of the lesser, though not all of them. Something is always lost in the joining.

A log dropped into a pool comes out changed into <color="#55FF55">Infused Wood</color>, and the pool remains. Stardust dropped in beside a crystal begins something stranger, which you will learn of in time.
The liquid sometimes reacts with its neighbours as well. Let it touch water and the starlight itself freezes solid into packed ice, leaving the water as it was. Let it touch lava and the starlight cools into sand, and now and then that sand holds enough light to become <color="#55FF55">Aquamarine Shale</color>.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.crystal: A crystal shaped into a tool holds its edge far better than any metal you have worked, and it cuts as deep as diamond. Any crystal will serve, though the tool takes after the crystals it was made from. A larger and cleaner cut crystal makes a stouter, quicker tool, so the ones you grew with care are worth spending here.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.infused:
Wood is a porous material, ripe for absorbing starlight. Drop a log into a pool of Liquid Starlight and it will drink the light into its grain, and what floats back up is <color="#55FF55">Infused Wood</color>. The pool is not used by this, so one pool will serve you for as many logs as you care to bring.
Cut it into planks and the forms that follow. Much of what you build from here, from focus relays to lenses and the tool that links them, will call for this wood in some shape or other.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.throwab:
Some of what starlight touches becomes restless, and a restless powder will do useful work when thrown. <color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> with a powder in hand to throw it, or <color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> a block to set it off in place. A dispenser can throw most of them for you.
<color="#55FF55">Illumination Powder</color> bursts into a hanging light that needs no torch and no wall. It will stay lit until you break it, and it leaves nothing behind when it goes.

<color="#55FF55">Nocturnal Powder</color> is the opposite, made deliberately. Where it lands it swallows the light for a short while, blinds anyone who stands too close, and calls monsters up out of the dark faster than the night ever would. In a world kept peaceful it calls nothing, though it still puts out the lights.
<color="#FF5555">Be warned, it will tear down every lamp, torch, and hanging light near it,</color> including your own. Throw it well away from anything you care about.

<color="#55FF55">Vivid Powder</color> is the kindest of these powders. Where it settles, the plants nearby grow as though seasons were passing in moments, and anything that ripens is gathered and set back into the soil on its own. Stand close and you will feel your own hurts mending while it lasts.
This one is too delicate for a dispenser to throw. You will have to do it by hand.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.cave_il:
You have seen how far a single hanging light reaches. The <color="#55FF55">Cave Illuminator</color> is for the dark beneath your feet.
Set it where it can see the sky, and set it with your own hands. From there it will send lights down into every dark, roofed hollow beneath it, layer by layer, deep into the ground. Nothing lit by day is touched.
The lights it places stay behind when it is removed, so place it with some thought.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.starmet:
Iron is a plain metal, but it is useful as a slate on which to inscribe celestial energy. Leave ore of it on open ground within the light of a <color="#55FFFF">focal point</color> and the starlight will work into it over time until it becomes <color="#55FF55">Starmetal Ore</color>. A pile of raw iron dropped in the same light becomes <color="#55FF55">Raw Starmetal</color>, though the raw metal is slower to turn than the stone.
Either one smelts in an ordinary furnace into a <color="#55FF55">Starmetal Ingot</color>.

The ingot is only half the value. Drop one on the ground and strike it with a <color="#55FF55">Starmetal Chisel</color>, and it will shed <color="#55FF55">Stardust</color>. The ingot is usually broken in the doing, so expect to feed it many ingots for a small heap of dust. A chisel touched by fortune wastes fewer.
You will use that dust more than almost anything else in this book. Start gathering it now.
Starmetal is hard, and it carries a faint light of its own, so a chisel made of it will disrupt the magical grain of a thing as well as the physical. The <color="#55FF55">Starmetal Chisel</color> is not swung at blocks. Drop the thing you mean to work on the ground, hold the chisel, and strike the fallen item. It will show itself ready to be struck while the chisel is in your hand.

Struck this way, a crystal will split. The new crystal takes a good share of the qualities of the parent with it, and some of those are lost in the breaking. A crystal that is too weak will not split at all.
An ingot of starmetal struck this way sheds stardust, and an artifact sheds a shard of itself.
The chisel accepts only the enchantments of durability and fortune, and fortune is the one worth having. It softens the losses in every use above.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.celesti:
A Rock Crystal has a ceiling to how fine it can become. To pass it, the crystal must be remade. Drop <color="#55FF55">Stardust</color> and a crystal together into a pool of Liquid Starlight over solid ground, and the pool will boil away and leave a small <color="#55FFFF">Celestial Crystal Cluster</color> where it stood.
The cluster grows on its own. It wants open sky, it grows quickest by night, and it grows faster still when rooted on Starmetal Ore, though the ore may be spent back into iron by the effort.

Give it time and it will swell through several stages until it shimmers. Break a full grown cluster with a pickaxe and it yields a <color="#55FF55">Celestial Crystal</color>, with stardust besides. Break it early and you will get dust at best, and nothing at all from a cluster that has only just formed.
A celestial crystal begins finer than any rock crystal and can be grown far further. It serves anywhere a rock crystal would, and it gives up starlight far more freely in a Lightwell.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.knowled:
You will not be the only one to walk this path, and there is no virtue in making a companion relearn what you already know. The <color="#55FF55">Scroll of Written Expertise</color> carries understanding from one mind to another.
<color="#FFFF55">Sneak + Right-click</color> with a blank scroll and your knowledge is set down on it under your name.

Another may then read it with a plain <color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> and receive the constellations you have seen and traced, the focal points you have found, and the depth of your understanding. The scroll gives and never takes, so a reader loses nothing they already had.
What is written cannot be rewritten, and you cannot read your own hand. The scroll is not used up by reading. It carries knowledge only, and nothing of the strength you have earned for yourself.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.focus_r:
A crafting table has only so many places for ingredients, and soon that will not be enough. The <color="#55FF55">Focus Relay</color> is a small pedestal that holds a single item raised in the air, and a table set among relays may draw from them as it works.
<color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> a relay with an item to set it there, and <color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> again with an empty hand to take it back. Keep the air above it clear, or it will throw the item off.

Relays are not linked by any tool. Their place is what matters. A table will search for them in a ring around itself, a short way out and level with it, and later in a wider ring set a little higher. Put them where the structure page for your next table shows and the table will find them.
The interface of the table shows you what each relay holds. When a process finishes, one item is taken from each relay it asked for.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.resonan:
Your first table was crafted to listen to celestial resonance. The next must be taught to work it into something more focused. Set a bucket of Liquid Starlight in the grid among the marble and crystal, and the illuminated table will remake itself where it stands into a <color="#55FF55">Resonating Crafting Table</color>. Your vision will widen again the moment it does.
The new table is a demanding thing. It will not work at all until it stands at the centre of the structure shown on the page that follows.

Sooty marble beneath, runed marble around it, and a ring of focus relays. When the structure is complete the floor will sparkle faintly. If you touch the table with the wand while something is out of place, the wand will show you what.
A wider form of the same structure, with a second ring of relays raised a little higher, will be asked for by the greatest works. Build the smaller one first.

Some recipes ask for more than the grid and the relays can hold. Items thrown on the ground near the table will be drawn up into the air and consumed as it works. Liquid Starlight is drawn from Containment Chalices within reach, a little at a time, until enough has been gathered.
All of it happens by night. Lay out your ingredients, fill the relays, and touch the table with the <color="#55FF55">Resonating Wand</color> once the dark has come.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.shootin:
Now that your understanding has deepened, the sky will begin to respond to it. Around the middle of the night, look up. Now and then a star will fall for you, a bright streak with a long tail, and it will come down somewhere not far off.
Chase it that same night. Whatever falls will be gone by dawn.

Where it lands you will find a small scatter of treasures, a crystal if you are close enough when it strikes, and something older than either. An <color="#55FFFF">Artifact</color>, which is a lesson of its own.
The star falls only in a world with an open sky above it. In a world roofed in stone, or one without stars, you will wait in vain.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.artifac:
So you have one. An <color="#55FFFF">Artifact</color> is not a tool and not a treasure, though it looks like both. It is a small bound will from somewhere very far from here, and it does not care for your pocket.
In your pack it sleeps. Drop it on the ground and it wakes, and from then on it belongs to you. It cannot be broken by any ordinary means and it will not fade away.

A woken artifact is restless. It will glow a colour and ring like a bell, and that is a riddle for you to solve. Something it wants must be brought near, or done to it, before the light fades. Hold it in mind and it will tell you what it wants, in its own way. Solve one riddle and it poses the next, and every riddle you have solved is stated plainly afterward.
Fail, and it grows unsettled. An unsettled artifact lashes out between riddles, calling monsters, hurling itself about, or vanishing to somewhere nearby.

Answer enough riddles and it settles. A settled artifact goes still and may be picked up and kept safely, and one day it will be spent to make something of yours greater than it was. Let it fall too far into unrest and it will tear itself apart. Do not ignore one you have woken.
Strike an artifact with your chisel and it sheds a shard of itself. Enough shards, worked at the table, become a small singularity. <color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> it, and keep doing so, until it has given up everything inside.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.formati:
Building by hand is honest work, and slow. The <color="#55FF55">Formation Wand</color> lays blocks for you in shapes, lines, walls, floors, and spheres, drawing the blocks from your own pack.
<color="#FFFF55">Sneak + Right-click</color> a block to teach the wand what to place. Teach it several kinds and it will mix them at random as it builds, for as long as you carry each. <color="#FFFF55">Sneak + Left-click</color> to make it forget.

<color="#FFFF55">Sneak + Right-click</color> the air to change its shape. A line running toward you from the face you touch, a line filling the space between you and what you are looking at, a flat plane, an upright wall, a solid sphere, or a hollow one.
<color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> a block face to build from it, or the open air to build where your gaze rests. The wand shows you a ghost of the shape before you commit. In time you will learn to fill the wand with lumen, and its reach will grow well beyond what it can extend to now.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.exchang:
Sometimes a thing is built of the wrong stone. The <color="#55FF55">Conversion Wand</color> trades one block for another without your having to tear the wall down first.
It is taught the same way as its sibling. <color="#FFFF55">Sneak + Right-click</color> a block to store it, <color="#FFFF55">Sneak + Left-click</color> to clear, and <color="#FFFF55">Sneak + Right-click</color> the air to change how much it will convert at once.

<color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> a block and the wand will spread from that spot across every connected block of the same kind that is open to the air, swapping each for one from your pack. The old blocks are broken properly, so nothing is lost. It will not touch what cannot be broken, nor anything harder than obsidian.
It converts only as many as you carry replacements for. Lumen, when you learn to fill it, will let it take on far more in a single stroke.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.starlig:
Not everything can be changed by a bath in Liquid Starlight alone. Some materials need the liquid pushed into them under pressure, and the <color="#55FF55">Starlight Infuser</color> is built for that. It draws from a ring of pools laid into the structure around it rather than from the sky, so it works day or night and under any roof.
<color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> the infuser with an item to set it in place, and again with an empty hand to take it back.

Every pool in the ring must be full of Liquid Starlight before the infuser will start, and they must stay full for the whole ritual. Touch the infuser with the <color="#55FF55">Resonating Wand</color> to begin. Liquid is drawn up from the pools into the item, and the result is thrown out on top when it finishes.
Each operation drains one pool block from the ring, so refill it between crafts. A Containment Chalice within reach will be drawn from instead, which spares the pools.
This is the process that refines Aquamarine into a <color="#55FF55">Resonating Gem</color>.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.tree_be:
Trees grow slowly, and felling them is slower still. The <color="#55FF55">Tree Beacon</color> replaces both. Place it on solid ground and grow a sapling anywhere inside the ring of light it casts. The tree that would have grown is taken up into the beacon instead, and a pale shadow of it is left standing in the air.
From then on the beacon works through the shadow, drawing out wood, leaves, and whatever else the tree would have given, and pours the harvest out around itself.

It works on its own at a steady pace. With open sky above it, starlight gathered through the night is spent on extra harvests. A beacon holding several trees works harder than one holding a single sapling, up to a point.
The shadow tree wears away very slowly and will need reseeding after a long while. Breaking the beacon returns every shadow to solid wood and leaf, so nothing is lost by moving it.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.enhance:
The ring of relays around your Resonating Crafting Table has room for only so much. The structure on the facing page widens it. A second ring of <color="#55FF55">Focus Relays</color> stands a step higher and farther out, greatly increasing what the table can draw on in a single recipe.
The table works without the wider form, so nothing you have built is wasted. But most of what remains in this chapter, and nearly all of the next, calls for the outer ring. Build it once and leave it standing.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.contain:
Buckets are a poor way to move Liquid Starlight in quantity. The <color="#55FF55">Containment Chalice</color> holds a great deal of any one liquid, suspended above the bowl where it can be seen. <color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> with a full container to pour in, or an empty one to draw out, and pipes may connect beneath it.
A chalice that is empty, or already holds Liquid Starlight, searches for Lightwells within a short distance and draws their Liquid Starlight across the air to itself, so long as nothing stands between them.

Altars and the Starlight Infuser search for chalices in the same way and take the liquid they need from any in reach, drawing from several at once when one is not enough.
Two chalices in sight of each other will react if their liquids can. Water and lava produce stone in its various forms. Liquid Starlight meeting water yields ice, and meeting lava it yields sand, with the occasional block of Aquamarine Shale. The product forms in the air between the two bowls. A redstone signal stops a chalice from doing any of this.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.celesti: Your work will spread across the world and beyond it in time, and walking will not do. The <color="#55FF55">Celestial Gateway</color> joins distant places through the sky itself. Every gateway that stands on its full structure with open sky above becomes a destination for every other, in this world or any other. In worlds that have no sky, the gateway treats the ceiling as open.

Step onto the plate. The world darkens around you and you find yourself beneath a dome of stars. Most are only background. The coloured ones are other gateways, set in their true direction if they share your world, and scattered across the dome if they do not. Gateways very close to the one you stand on are not shown. Look at one and its name appears beside it, if it was given one.

Hold <color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> or <color="#FFFF55">Sneak</color> while looking at a star, keep your gaze on it, and after a moment you will be carried there. The crossing costs nothing.
Name the gateway on an anvil or dye it before placing, and that is how its star will appear to others.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.luminou:
The Resonating table can be raised once more, in place, into the <color="#55FF55">Luminous Crafting Altar</color>. The recipe calls for the full outer ring of relays, Stardust thrown on the ground nearby, and Liquid Starlight drawn from chalices, so have all three ready. When it finishes the table is replaced where it stands and your vision widens again.
The larger structure on the facing page must be completed before the new altar will work.

This altar has one thing its predecessors did not. Beside the grid in its interface is a slot for a <color="#55FFFF">constellation focus</color>. An <color="#55FF55">Attuned Crystal</color> set there attunes the recipe to that one constellation, and many recipes from here on will not begin without the right one in place.
Some of those processes are hard on the focus and will shatter the crystal when they complete. The recipe pages tell you which.
Its work is still done by night, and the wand still begins it.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.blink_w:
The <color="#55FF55">Traversal Wand</color> moves you. It has two forms, and <color="#FFFF55">Sneak + Right-click</color> switches between them.
In its first form, hold <color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> to gather force and release to be thrown in the direction you are looking. The longer you hold, the farther you go, and the ground will not hurt you when you land.
In its second form, a line is drawn from you to the point you are looking at while you hold, and releasing carries you straight to it.

The second form will not take you anywhere too close to where you already stand, and it reaches only so far. Aim at open sky and you will arrive in the air at the end of the line.
Both forms share a short rest between uses. The wand works with nothing inside it. Filled with Vicio lumen, both forms grow considerably in reach, and a little lumen is spent with each use.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.impulsi: The <color="#55FF55">Impulsion Wand</color> throws a hook. <color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> to cast it along your line of sight. It falls as it flies, so a long cast will need to be aimed high. When the hook takes hold of a block you are hauled to it, with a small lift at the start to clear the edge.

When it takes hold of a creature you are pulled to the creature instead, wherever it moves. A hook that finds nothing fades. You take no harm from falling while the line is pulling you, and the wand needs a short rest between casts. It costs nothing else.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.constel:
Starlight of a single constellation, applied to a living thing over time, leaves a lasting change. The clearest example is a flower. A small flower planted on open ground at a <color="#55FFFF">focal point</color> will be remade over time into a bloom that carries that constellation's signature, and a small flower dropped there as an item will change the same way, more slowly.
Each focal point produces only the flower of its own constellation.

<color="#55FF55">Hyacinth</color> carries Aevitas. <color="#55FF55">Orchid</color> carries Armara. <color="#55FF55">Thistle</color> carries Discidia. <color="#55FF55">Protea</color> carries Evorsio. <color="#55FF55">Iris</color> carries Vicio.
As plants they are ordinary and will sit in a pot like any other. Their value is as a catalyst. Placed in a <color="#55FF55">Lumen Array</color>, each flower releases the energy it carries as <color="#55FFFF">lumen</color>, a form of starlight that has taken on a single aspect and can be stored, moved, and bound into the things you carry.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.lumen_a:
The <color="#55FF55">Lumen Array</color> turns Liquid Starlight into <color="#55FFFF">lumen</color> of one type. <color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> it with a bucket of Liquid Starlight to fill it, then with a constellation flower to seat the catalyst. From then on it works on its own, drinking the liquid slowly and filling its own reserve with the lumen of that flower.
Once it has produced one type it accepts only catalysts of that type. Build a separate array for each.

Look at the array and its contents are shown beside your crosshair. It works fastest when its reserve is about half full and slows as it nears empty or full, so an array nobody draws from settles into a slow idle. It releases lumen to other devices only once it holds a fair amount.
The flower will shatter in time and must be replaced. A redstone signal stops the array from producing, though it still sips starlight and the flower may still shatter. A comparator reads how much it holds. It needs no structure and no sky.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.lumen_f:
Lumen does not flow through pipes. It passes through open air between devices that can see one another a short way off. Arrays offer lumen, other devices request it, and the request is answered along the shortest clear path.
The <color="#55FF55">Lumen Filament</color> extends that reach. Set filaments where each can see the next and they will pass a request from one to the next until it finds an array holding what was asked for. A filament stores nothing, and for a moment after each transfer it lights in the colour of what passed through it.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.lumen_c:
Lumen in a reserve is useful. Lumen in your hand is more so. The <color="#55FF55">Lumen Crystallizer</color> draws lumen from nearby arrays and Liquid Starlight from its own tank and grows the two together into a solid <color="#55FFFF">Lumen Crystal Cluster</color> on its upper plate.
<color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> it with Liquid Starlight to fill it and with a catalyst to seat it. The catalyst decides which lumen the crystallizer requests. Once the cluster forms, the catalyst is used up.

A sapling calls for Aevitas, an ingot for Armara, an arrow for Discidia, a stone for Evorsio, and a feather for Vicio. Any crystal of yours calls for Prismatic lumen, which you will meet later.
Break the cluster by hand and it yields a <color="#55FF55">Lumen Crystal</color> and shrinks by one stage rather than vanishing, so a fed crystallizer keeps giving. A lumen crystal seated as the catalyst requests its own type and never shatters, which is the way to keep one running.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.lumen_b:
A <color="#55FF55">Lumen Crystal</color> is starlight of one aspect made solid, and it can be pressed into the things you carry. Throw a lumen crystal, a piece of <color="#55FF55">Stardust</color>, and the item together into a pool of Liquid Starlight. The item comes out bound to that lumen and charged with it.
Armour, weapons, mining tools, and a filled Stardew flask can all be bound. An item holds one bound aspect at a time, and a new binding replaces the old. Only the flask keeps every binding it is given.

A binding works while the item is in use, worn or held, and while it still holds a charge. Using the item in the way its aspect favours spends the charge. Throw the item back into a pool with another lumen crystal of the same type to refill it.
<color="#55FF55">Aevitas</color> lengthens life and is fed by the harm you take. <color="#55FF55">Armara</color> hardens armour and turns blows aside, fed the same way. <color="#55FF55">Discidia</color> sharpens every strike and is fed by the harm you deal.

<color="#55FF55">Evorsio</color> quickens the breaking of blocks and is fed by breaking them. On a weapon it pierces armour instead. <color="#55FF55">Vicio</color> speeds your step and is fed by walking, and on a bow it speeds the arrow instead.
<color="#55FF55">Stardew</color> is a flask filled from a cauldron of water. Bound with a lumen it takes on that aspect's effect as a drink, and further bindings stack more effects into the same flask. Each flask holds a few sips before it must be filled and bound again.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.attunem:
Until now you have used starlight of every constellation at once. Filtering it down to one changes what it can do, and it can be turned on a person as well as a crystal. The <color="#55FF55">Attunement Altar</color> is that filter. It stands at the centre of a wide plaza of sooty marble, all of it under open sky, shown on the facing page.
The plaza itself is only the frame. The pattern that does the work is laid out by you.

Place <color="#55FF55">Focus Relays</color> on the floor in the shape of a constellation, its stars traced small around the altar. Hold a Constellation Paper for that constellation near the altar at night and the floor will show you where each relay belongs. When the pattern is complete and the constellation is in the sky, light will run between the relays along its lines.
Any constellation overhead will respond to its pattern, but the altar will only attune you to one you have discovered.

Stand on the altar at night while the pattern is lit, and do not sneak. The starlight will settle into you over a short while, and afterward you are <color="#55FFFF">attuned</color> to that constellation. This opens the Perks section of this book and the first perk of that constellation's path. It can be done only once unless the attunement is later removed.
Drop a Rock Crystal or Celestial Crystal onto the altar under the same conditions and it is lifted, turned in the light, and set down as an <color="#55FF55">Attuned Crystal</color> of that constellation.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.perk_ge:
Attunement changes you, and you will find a map of it under the Perks bookmark. Each constellation begins its own path, and the paths meet farther out. Points to spend on it come from acting in the way your constellation favours. Aevitas grows through building, Armara through enduring harm, Discidia through dealing it, Evorsio through breaking, and Vicio through travel.
Some places on the map are sockets, and those take a <color="#55FF55">Dynamism Gem</color>.

Throw Illumination Powder and a crystal together into a pool of Liquid Starlight and a gem cluster forms. It grows under open sky through a few stages, and the time of day at its last step decides what it becomes. Grown by day it is an <color="#55FF55">Ilium</color> gem, with more and weaker qualities. Grown by night it is a <color="#55FF55">Fengarum</color> gem, with fewer and stronger ones.

Grown at dawn or dusk it is an <color="#55FF55">Ourium</color> gem, between the two. Harvest it at full size, since it will shrink again if left.
<color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> a socket you have unlocked and choose a gem from those you carry. <color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> a filled socket to take the gem out.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.shiftin:
An attunement is not a permanent mark. The <color="#55FF55">Shifting Star</color> removes it. Hold <color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> for a few moments and the star breaks, taking with it your attuned constellation, every perk you have chosen, and all the experience behind them.
You are then free to return to the Attunement Altar and choose again. Consider what you are giving up before you use it. More refined stars exist that change the constellation while keeping the experience you have earned, and you will learn to make them in time.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.perk_to: Some perks on the map are only stepping stones to what lies past them, and some are useful only now and then. The <color="#55FF55">Perk Seal</color> suppresses one without removing it. In the Perks section, drag a seal from your stock in the corner onto a perk. The perk stays allocated and still carries the path onward, but its effect stops. Double-click a sealed perk to break the seal. The seal is spent either way.

The <color="#55FF55">Perk Nullifier</color> goes further and removes a perk entirely, returning the point to you to spend elsewhere. Drag one onto the perk in the same way. Hold <color="#FFFF55">Ctrl</color> while dragging either tool to apply several in a row.
A perk cannot be removed while others depend on it for their connection back to the root, nor while it is sealed. The nullifier is spent on use.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.starlig:
An attuned crystal holds the signature of one constellation. Set into a crystal lattice, it becomes a source. The <color="#55FF55">Starlight Focus Crystal</color> provdes this, and keeps every quality of the crystal you set into it, so choose a large and well cut one. Those two qualities decide how much light it gives.
It must stand in the column of a <color="#55FFFF">focal point</color> whose constellation matches its own. Height does not matter, only the column.

Set correctly, it shows a wide fan of light in the colour of its constellation whenever it can see the sky, and the beam of the focal point itself becomes visible to the bare eye. Anyone standing near it is able to fly for as long as they stay close.
By night, while its constellation is overhead, it gives off a steady flow of that constellation's starlight. The flow follows the moon. On nights when the constellation is absent, nothing flows.

The flow must be linked to a target with the <color="#55FF55">Linking Tool</color>, and each link needs a clear line of sight over a short distance. Several links share the flow between them.
Point it at a crafting altar and the altar receives that starlight for the consumers that call for it. Point it at a Tree Beacon or a Celestial Crystal Cluster and they will work faster. Point it at a plain block and the light will reform certain blocks in ways a bare focal point cannot.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.lens_pr:
A source reaches only a short way, and always in a straight line. To carry starlight farther, or around an obstacle, it must be relayed. The <color="#55FF55">Lens</color> takes starlight in from any number of links and passes it on to a single target. It hangs from whatever face you place it against and turns to face the target it is given.
A lens is made around a crystal, and a larger crystal yields several lenses from one working.

The <color="#55FF55">Prism</color> does the opposite of the lens. It takes starlight in and divides it evenly among as many targets as it has been linked to.
Both are built around a crystal, and here purity is the quality that counts. A perfectly pure crystal passes on everything it receives. Each missing step of purity strips away a share of the flow at every relay it passes through, and a long chain of poor relays loses most of what it might carry.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.linking:
Starlight sources and relays do not connect on their own. You must join them, and the <color="#55FF55">Linking Tool</color> allows you to do that.
<color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> a source or relay to select it. While it is selected, streams of light show every link already established. <color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> a second block to link the first to it, or <color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> a block already linked to remove that link. <color="#FFFF55">Left-click</color> anywhere to stop, and putting the tool away does the same.

A link will not form over too great a distance, nor through anything that blocks the view between the two ends. If something is built into the path later, that link goes dark until the path is cleared again, once clear it doesn't need relinking.
A lens accepts only one outgoing link. A prism and a focus crystal accept as many as you care to make, and the flow is shared equally among them, so remove links you no longer need.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.radianc:
The last raising of the altar, in place, into the <color="#55FF55">Iridescent Crafting Altar</color>. This creation draws on everything you have built. It needs each of the five basic lumen carried in over the lumen network, Armara starlight carried in over the starlight network, powders and stardust thrown to the ground, and Liquid Starlight from chalices.
It also needs an Armara focus in the slot, and that focus will not survive the process.

The structure grows outward once more, with a further ring of sooty and runed marble and four low pillars at the corners. When the starlight finishes, the altar is replaced where it stands and your vision widens for the last time this book can offer.
Few tasks need this altar. Those that do are found in the final chapter, and most of them reshape things already made.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.lumen_a:
Lumen of one aspect can be combined with lumen of another to make something neither is alone. The <color="#55FF55">Lumen Alchemy Array</color> does this. It is fed like the plain array, with Liquid Starlight and a catalyst, but it also draws lumen of other types from arrays within a short distance that can see it.
Filaments cannot carry lumen into an alchemy array. Each feeding array must stand within reach of it directly.

The catalyst decides what is made, and the array will not accept a catalyst until it holds starlight and can match the catalyst to a recipe. If any one of the lumen types a recipe needs is missing, nothing is made until it is supplied.
Higher aspects drink more starlight and wear out their catalysts faster. Like the plain array, it is assigned to the first lumen it produces and to no other, works best when about half full, is stopped by redstone, and releases what it holds only once it has gathered a fair amount.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.complex:
The five basic aspects are only the beginning. Combined in an alchemy array they yield a second rank of lumen, and that rank combined again yields a third, and the third, taken all together, yields <color="#55FF55">Prismatic</color> lumen, starlight with every aspect restored at once.
Each new lumen has bindings of its own, stronger and stranger than the aspects it was made from. The Lumen bookmark of this book records every lumen you have produced, with its making and its bindings.

<color="#55FF55">Virel</color> joins life to motion. <color="#55FF55">Solyn</color> joins life to defence and marks whatever it strikes. <color="#55FF55">Caldor</color> joins force to defence and to breaking, and an arrow bound with it never strays. <color="#55FF55">Nullae</color> joins breaking to motion and makes a miner faster in every way.
These four are the second rank, each made from the basic aspects in an alchemy array.

From the second rank, each pair joined with one basic aspect, come <color="#55FF55">Hyle</color>, which shields and mends, <color="#55FF55">Dynamis</color>, which strikes harder and faster and bursts on a killing blow, <color="#55FF55">Aion</color>, which shortens every wait and lengthens your blessings whenever you are struck, and <color="#55FF55">Akasha</color>, which extends your reach and gathers what you mine into a single bundle.
<color="#55FF55">Prismatic</color> lumen is made from all four of those. Bound alongside another lumen, it strengthens that binding and costs nothing to keep. It is also the price of the greatest manipulations of starlight in this book.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.illumin:
The <color="#55FF55">Illumination Wand</color> makes light where you point it. <color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> a block face to set a small hanging light there, and <color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> that light again to remove it. The colour is set by crafting the wand together with a dye.
<color="#FFFF55">Sneak + Right-click</color> a solid block and it becomes a ghost of itself in the colour of the wand, and you can see through it. <color="#FFFF55">Sneak + Right-click</color> it again to restore it. Only the one who made the ghost can undo it.

<color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> a Cave Illuminator with the wand and the illuminator takes on the colour of the wand and works many times faster for a good while afterward, with a ring of light spinning around it while it does.
The wand has no cost to use and does not wear out.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.iridesc:
A crystal tool can be raised further by a alteration at the Luminous altar, with a focus of a particular constellation for each tool, shown on its recipe page. The focus is destroyed each time, so an attuned crystal is part of the price. The tool comes back <color="#55FFFF">iridescent</color>, with an ability of its own.
The <color="#55FF55">Iridescent Crystal Pickaxe</color> breaks a wide face of stone at once. <color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> and it reveals every ore within a short distance, marked in light. It needs a rest between uses.

The <color="#55FF55">Iridescent Crystal Axe</color> reaches farther than an ordinary tool, and when it breaks one log of a tree, the whole tree comes down with it. Hold <color="#FFFF55">Sneak</color> while chopping to take a single log instead. Felling a tree needs a short rest before the next.

The <color="#55FF55">Iridescent Crystal Shovel</color> breaks a wide face like the pickaxe, and when it breaks one block it follows the vein, taking every connected block of the same kind up to a good distance. Hold <color="#FFFF55">Sneak</color> to dig a single block. It too needs a short rest after a vein.

The <color="#55FF55">Iridescent Crystal Sword</color> strikes truer than any blade before it, and it can be charged. Hold <color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> a moment and release to send a crescent of force through everything ahead of you. Hold until the charge is full and release to call a <color="#55FFFF">Celestial Strike</color> down on whatever you are looking at, a burst of stellar force against everything near the point of impact.

Both strikes are strongest under open stars, and every rest between uses is halved by night.
The full strike takes after your attunement. Discidia makes it crueler. Aevitas heals you and those near you. Armara shields you. Vicio carries you to the point of impact. Evorsio throws everything around you away from you.
While the sword is charging, missiles aimed at you are turned back on their sender. Turn one back in the first instant of charging and your next release is a full strike.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.resplen:
A Shifting Star resonates without pattern, which is what lets it break an attunement. Held still in filtered starlight and set into an Eye of Ender, that resonance can be made to reach outward instead. The <color="#55FF55">Resplendent Prism</color> is the result, worn at the neck.
While worn, it raises the enchantments on whatever else you hold and wear. The bonuses it gives are decided when it is made and cannot be chosen.

A prism holds a small number of bonuses. Some add levels to an enchantment you already have. Some grant an enchantment the item does not have at all. Rarely, one raises every enchantment on an item together.
If the bonuses are not to your liking, the prism can be returned to the altar and remade. The old bonuses are lost in the remaking and new ones are rolled in their place.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.attuned:
The plain Shifting Star breaks an attunement and everything built on it. These refined stars are gentler. Each one is bound to a single constellation, and using it carries you across to that constellation while keeping all the experience you have earned.
Hold <color="#FFFF55">Right-click</color> for a few moments. Your perks are unbound and must be chosen again along the new path, but nothing else is lost. The star is spent. You must have been attuned before and have discovered the constellation it carries.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.stellar:
A focal point with its focus crystal in place can be made brighter still. The <color="#55FF55">Stellar Filament</color> is a small pillar and it's purpose is its placement. Set filaments around a focus crystal in the pattern its constellation calls for and the crystal recognises them as a layer.
Every layer widens and brightens the column of light rising from the focal point, until it can be seen from a great distance without any glass.

A layer is four filaments on the same level, one in each diagonal quarter around the crystal, none in line with it, and no two ever stacked in the same column.
A correct layer draws itself in light. Holding a filament fades that light so you can see what you are placing.\nIn a fortuitous turn of events, placed active starlight focus crystals grant an area of flight around themselves, which may help facilitate building these filament layers.

Each constellation adds a rule of its own.
Aevitas requires pairs directly across from one another, but not four of them set as a square.
Armara requires a mirror on one side only.
Discidia forbids any square corner.
Evorsio forbids any turned symmetry, so no filament may sit a quarter turn or a half turn from another.
Vicio requires all four at different distances.
tome.research.node.astralsorcery.artifac:
A settled artifact has one final use, and it is the reason to settle one. Thrown to the ground beside the Iridescent altar, with a great deal of Prismatic lumen and Liquid Starlight on hand, it is consumed to make one of your own things more than it was.
An enchanted item comes back with its enchantments raised, save curses and those that have only one level. A Resplendent Prism comes back with a further bonus. A Dynamism Gem comes back with a further quality.

Whatever is enhanced this way becomes unique. It takes a name of its own kind and a rarity beyond any other, and it can never be enhanced a second time.
This is the last technique this book has to teach. What you make of it is yours.
